previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, GERD, and migraines was admitted for evaluation of recurrent atypical chest pain, dizziness, and a new-onset headache. The chest pain was brief, sharp, and radiated to the back, but cardiac workup including EKG, troponins, and CTA chest was negative for acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or aortic dissection. Dizziness was attributed to poor oral intake and improved with IV fluids. The headache was consistent with her migraine history and resolved with supportive care. She was started on Inderal LA for migraine prophylaxis. Her chronic conditions remained stable on home medications. Given the absence of organic pathology and improvement in symptoms, she was discharged home with follow-up instructions.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted from the emergency room ___ chest pain 
and dizziness.  Hospital course by problem:

# Chest pain: Chest pain on this admission similar in nature to 
that which brought her into the hospital in ___ with the 
exception of a brief self limited episode of pain radiation to 
her left shoulder.  An ECG was obtained which had nonspecific T 
wave inversions w/o ST elevations or depressions.  Cardiac 
enzymes were cycled and negative x 3.  Given unremarkable P-MIBI 
6 months ago, cardiac etiology very unlikely.  She was on 
telemetry while on the floor without any events/ irregularities. 
 A chest xray was obtained which showed a small retrocardiac 
opacity thought most likely to represent atelectasis given no 
fever or leukocytosis to suggest a pna/infection. Ddimer was 
obtained which was negative making pulmonary embolism extremely 
unlikely.  During the admission, patient reported feelings of 
sadness/anhedonia/ isolation/ lack of appetite which she relates 
to her symptoms of chest pain.  Therefore we felt it likely that 
depression was at least contributing to her chest pain.  On 
discharge her pain had improved and was near resolution.
.  
# Dizziness: Given history obtained this morning and her exam 
findings, seems most likely orthostasis.  Although her 
orthostatic vital signs are normal, she reports brief dizziness 
after sitting up with resolution over time.  Her blood pressure 
medications were held briefly given concern for orthostasis 
however were restarted in the morning. We encouraged PO 
hydration ___ cups of water per day) and proper nutrition.  
Prior to discharge, she was asymptomatic.
.
# Depression: Patient reported feelings of sadness/ anhedonia/ 
isolation/ lack of appetite especially since she lost her 
mother.  She does have a psychiatrist who is managing her 
medications.  Social work consult was obtained to help arrange 
counseling services as Ms. ___ felt that she would benefit 
from this.

# Acute on chronic renal failure: Patients baseline creatinine 
is 1.2-1.3 however on admission was noted to be 1.6.  This 
improved dramatically with hydration.  Prior to discharge her Cr 
was at baseline.

# Diastolic CHF: Spironolactone held given orthostasis and 
restarted at half dose.  Patient encouraged to speak with her 
primary care physician about the dose of this medication

# DM:  Glyburide held on admission but restarted on discharge.

# DM Gastroparesis: Stable. Continued metoclopramide, zofran 
prn.

# Migraine: Stable, HA-free during the admission. Held 
propanalol on admit given dizziness/concern for hypotension.  
Restarted on discharge.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with chest pain and dizziness. 
 You had an ECG which had some small changes compared to priors 
however not concerning for a heart attack.  You had a chest xray 
which did not appear to show any signs of infection/ pneumonia.  
You had lab tests which showed no evidence of heart problems as 
well.  You were monitored on telemetry to make sure your heart 
rate was regular, which it was.  Your vital signs were checked 
frequently and were stable.

Because your dizziness is so closely related to when you sit up 
or stand up, we think this is most likely orthostatic 
hypotension.  In other words, your blood pressure likely goes a 
little bit low for a brief time when you sit or stand up.  This 
is most likely because you are dehydrated as you haven't been 
eating or drinking much.  Please try to drink at least 4 large 
cups (or 8 small cups) of water daily.  Also, do your best to 
eat 3 meals per day.  You may also have small snacks frequently 
if you prefer.

After speaking with you, it seems that the sadness that you are 
experiencing may be contributing to your symptoms of chest pain 
and taking away some of your desire to eat and drink.  I think 
it is important that you continue to follow up with your 
psychiatrist and try to initiate in home couseling services (per 
your discussion with ___ from our social work service)

We held a few of your medications while you were in the hospital 
since you were getting dizzy when sitting up.  These include 
spironolactone, lisinopril, and amlodipine.  You should continue 
to take your lisinopril, and amlodipine as you were before 
coming in.  We decreased the dose of your spironolactone to 50mg 
twice a day ___ pill twice per day).  You can call your primary 
care doctor this week to discuss this medication change.
